controls.title: Enforce usable password standards
controls.statement: Require passwords and passphrases of appropriate length, allow long and usable values, prevent reuse, and avoid composition rules that encourage predictable choices.
controls.risk: Attackers may guess or crack short, reused or predictable passwords and use them to impersonate trusted users across several systems.
controls.scope: Human and non-human accounts that use passwords for single-factor or multi-factor authentication, including verifier configuration and password changes.
controls.examine: Compare password standards with configured minimum and maximum lengths, accepted characters, composition rules, history and reuse settings for representative identity stores and applications.
controls.interview: Ask identity and service owners how requirements differ by authentication type, how unsupported applications are handled and how usability problems are prevented from creating workarounds.
controls.test: Use authorised test accounts to attempt short, reused and long valid passwords, confirming that prohibited values fail and supported passphrases work consistently across sign-in and reset paths.
test_steps: Select representative identity stores and applications using passwords alone and with MFA, including sign-in, change, reset and administrative creation paths.
Attempt values below the required minimum, at the minimum, long passphrases, all supported printable characters and a password used by another sampled account.
Confirm prohibited values and reuse are rejected consistently while valid long passwords work without truncation or hidden composition requirements.
Inspect effective verifier policy and exception records and remove or reset all test credentials after recording the actual outcomes.
controls.expected: Password controls enforce approved length and reuse rules, support long usable values and do not depend on predictable composition patterns.

mappings.basis: Requires a minimum of 15 characters for single-factor passwords on non-classified, OFFICIAL: Sensitive and PROTECTED systems.
Requires password maximum lengths to support at least 64 characters.
Requires support for all printable ASCII characters in passwords.
Sets minimum lengths for passwords used in single-factor and multi-factor authentication.
Recommends support for password lengths of at least 64 characters.
Requires unique passwords across enterprise assets and gives length guidance based on MFA use.
Requires password strength and reuse restrictions to be defined and enforced.
Requires password strength and reuse restrictions to be defined and enforced.

controls.title: Block compromised passwords and guessing attacks
controls.statement: Reject common, expected and compromised passwords, monitor repeated failures, and limit automated guessing without creating unsafe recovery paths.
controls.risk: A password spraying or automated guessing attack could compromise accounts at scale without needing to steal individual credentials.
controls.scope: Password creation and reset, compromised-password data, password filters, authentication failure controls, lockout or rate limiting and account recovery.
controls.examine: Inspect password-filter sources and update dates, blocked-value policy, failed-authentication telemetry, rate limits, lockout settings, recovery controls and exception handling.
controls.interview: Ask identity and monitoring teams how compromised-password intelligence is updated, spraying is detected and locked or attacked accounts are safely recovered.
controls.test: Attempt authorised creation of common and known-compromised passwords, then perform a controlled sequence of failed sign-ins and verify rejection, throttling or lockout, alerting and safe recovery.
test_steps: Confirm the password filter uses a current source of common, expected and compromised values and applies to creation, change, reset and administrative assignment.
Attempt authorised selection of representative blocked passwords, including organisation-specific predictable terms, and verify rejection without revealing unnecessary detail.
Perform a controlled sequence of failed sign-ins across one account and several accounts to exercise guessing and password-spraying protections.
Verify throttling or lockout, central event and alert creation, safe account recovery and documented handling for any exempt break-glass identity.
controls.expected: Known weak passwords cannot be selected, automated guessing is constrained and visible, and recovery does not restore access without appropriate identity checks.

mappings.basis: Prohibits passwords found in commonly used or compromised-password lists.
Requires maintained common and compromised-password lists, password filtering, protected transmission and storage, and secure post-recovery changes.
Requires a password-filtering solution for all user accounts as part of account management and monitoring.
Requires controls against online guessing and limits consecutive failed authentication attempts.
Requires user objects, other than break-glass accounts, to lock after no more than five failed logon attempts.

controls.title: Protect stored and managed passwords
controls.statement: Keep passwords out of readable stores, use approved password managers or resistant salted password hashing, and protect transmission and administrative access to credential stores.
controls.risk: One exposed document, database or credential vault could reveal reusable passwords and turn a local compromise into widespread unauthorised access.
controls.scope: Password managers, application databases, configuration, documents, shared locations, transmission channels, salts, password hashing and administrative access.
controls.examine: Review password-manager architecture and access, searches for readable credentials, application password-storage schemes, salts and work factors, protected transmission and migration plans for obsolete hashes.
controls.interview: Ask identity, application and platform owners how passwords enter approved stores, how exposed credentials are found and changed and how vault administrators are controlled and monitored.
controls.test: Sample applications and shared repositories for readable passwords, inspect representative stored verifiers and transmission paths, and verify that managed passwords are generated, access-controlled and auditable.
test_steps: Select applications, password vaults, configuration stores, shared repositories and transmission paths that create, hold or use passwords.
Inspect stored verifiers for unique salts, approved password hashing and work factors, and confirm cleartext or reversibly encrypted passwords are absent.
Use a controlled marker to search shared files, scripts, logs and collaboration locations and verify discovery and response for readable credentials.
Generate and retrieve a managed password through an authorised user, verify access control and audit logging, then rotate it and confirm the old value no longer works.
controls.expected: Passwords are not recoverable from ordinary storage, approved managers protect necessary shared secrets, and verifier data and transmission resist offline theft and interception.

mappings.basis: Requires stored credentials to use a password manager, hardware security module, or salted, hashed and stretched database storage.
Requires passwords to be transmitted over protected channels and stored with an approved salted key-derivation function.
Requires password managers to generate and manage passwords and protect the passwords they hold.
Requires per-password salts and resistant password hashing with scheme and work-factor information retained for migration.
Calls for centrally managed password storage, individual monitored vault access and discovery of readable passwords in shared content.
